blocks.text: Understanding Gemini

Think about the last time you had to make sense of scattered information — emails from three different people, the notes you took, a PDF report, and some reading materials that you barely touched. And, the most challenging part is that you need to go through all of this as soon as possible.

If this sounds familiar, the Gemini is what you need. Its strength lies in handling exactly such challenges, and you will learn how in this guide!

blocks.text: Meet Gemini

Gemini is Google's AI assistant that excels at synthesis work.

That is, not only can it process multiple inputs together and reason across them to answer complex questions, but it is also arguably the best choice for this type of task!
Gemini works with four main types of input:

• Screenshots and photos
  • Various document formats (PDFs, Docs, etc.)
  • Tables and CSVs
  • Plain text
Choosing the right format increases clarity and reduces guesswork.

blocks.text: How Gemini Works
Let's see this in practice. Imagine you're preparing for an important meeting and you have scattered information:

• A few documents with key details
  • Email threads with different people
  • Some notes you took earlier
  • Screenshots or images related to the topic
Normally, you'd open each file separately, read through everything, and try to remember how it all connects. That takes time and mental energy.

However, with Gemini, you can upload everything at once and ask one question: "Based on everything here, what are the main points I need to know?" After that, Gemini will read across all your materials and give you a synthesized answer.

Gemini Features
What makes Gemini capable of handling complex tasks efficiently is its features. One of these features is Modes:

• Flash mode — for high-volume, everyday tasks
  • Thinking mode — for complex problems that need careful analysis
  • Pro mode — for advanced technical challenges
Each mode is created to approach different kinds of work in the most optimized way.

So, you can match the mode to your task's complexity.

This flexibility means Gemini adapts to what you're doing, not the other way around.
Apart from modes, Gemini also offers specialized tools for different types of work:

• Create Image and Create Video — generate visual content from prompts
  • Create Music — produce original music
  • Deep Research — multi-step research with structured summaries
  • Canvas — draft and refine longer documents
  • Guided Learning — interactive, step-by-step explanations

In this course, you'll explore three powerful Gemini capabilities: image creation, music generation, and deep research. Together, they help you unlock your creativity and tackle complex questions with more depth and confidence. All of these features are available in the free version of Gemini, while video generation is exclusive to Pro users.
In turn, if you're also interested in creating videos with Gemini, then you can check out our guide about Omni after completing this one!
Where Gemini Has Limits
Last but not least, even the newest AI models have blind spots, so you need to know about it too. For example, Gemini:

• Might not know about every recent event
  • Can sometimes make guesses when it's unsure
  • Takes more time for complex tasks
  • Should not replace human judgment when making decisions
Therefore, you need to always keep these things in mind while using Gemini and other AI tools.

By the end of this lesson, you'll know how to turn raw notes into clear drafts, reshape text without losing meaning, adapt it for any audience, and produce ready-to-use writing for work or personal projects. Let's go!
From Notes to Narrative

Most writing begins as fragments — bullet points, half sentences, messy thoughts. Gemini is designed to help you turn those fragments into something that feels coherent and intentional.

Instead of rewriting everything yourself, you can hand Gemini your roughest notes and ask it to build the skeleton of a draft. Then you shape, refine, and guide it.
Why Gemini Works Well With Notes
Raw notes contain the essentials: key points, ideas, and moments of clarity. Gemini can detect:

• Relationships between ideas
  • Missing transitions
  • Implied structure
  • Natural ordering
  • Opportunities for clarity
This makes it easy to turn scattered thinking into something presentable.
From Notes to a Draft

blocks.text: One Step at a Time
Notice how much cleaner that is? The key is thinking in layers when you write your prompt:

1. Content — the raw ideas.
  2. Structure — the order and grouping.
  3. Style — tone, clarity, pacing.
  4. Format — bullets, paragraphs, summaries, scripts, etc.
A strong prompt doesn't demand perfection — it guides Gemini through these layers.
Giving Gemini the Right Signals
The more context you give, the better the result. Useful signals to include:

• The audience (manager, customer, friend, general reader)
  • The format (email, brief, summary, article, post)
  • The purpose (inform, persuade, clarify, summarize)
  • Length level (short, medium, long)
This makes Gemini's first draft much closer to what you need.

blocks.text: Improving Existing Writing

Drafting from scratch isn't the only thing Gemini can do. Got something written but not quite right? Gemini can clarify meaning, simplify dense passages, tighten loose sentences, adjust tone, improve flow, or fix grammar.

You stay in control — Gemini helps you explore possibilities.
Deep Research for Meaningful Writing

Gemini can do more than polish your sentences — it can help you think. Deep Research helps Gemini combine insights, patterns, examples, and context to strengthen your ideas. As a result, you get a more thoughtful, structured output based on either Gemini's sources (web or Workspace search) or files you upload.
You can ask Gemini to:

• Explore different angles or interpretations
  • Surface the core tension or opportunity in your topic
  • Expand points with relevant explanations
  • Identify assumptions, contradictions, or missing context
  • Propose stronger framing for your message
This is how you move from "well-written text" to meaningful, well-developed copy your audience can trust and learn from.
Tone and Audience Adaptation

Tone matters as much as content. You can ask Gemini to rewrite text in styles such as: professional, friendly, direct, neutral, analytical, motivational; or tailored to audiences like teammates, customers, executives, or learners.

Create Without Knowing Code

Hey! Today, you'll learn how to build simple, visual things with Gemini — even if you've never written code before. Gemini can turn plain descriptions or rough sketches into clean code, explain what it does, and help you improve it using everyday language. And you can use it as a starting point to build a website — no coding background needed!
Tech Tasks Made Simple

Let's put it this way: code is simply instructions written for a computer. Gemini's job here is to translate your words into a language the computer understands — and back: from machine instructions into human words you get.
Beginner-Friendly HTML/CSS
HTML and CSS are the simplest parts of coding because you can see what each part does.

• HTML describes what shows up on a page
  • CSS describes how it looks — colors, layouts, spacing
You don't need to write these languages yourself. Gemini does the technical part; you guide the design.
Describe What You Want
To create something, you don't need technical instructions. You can simply say:

• "Make a centered title with a short paragraph below it."
  • "Add a friendly button at the bottom."
  • "Create a section with three cards in a row."
Gemini turns these plain descriptions into working code.

blocks.prompt: Complete a prompt that turns a description into code.
blocks.template: Create a simple [output type] based on my [input type], and include clean HTML and CSS that [output details].

blocks.text: Describe a Simple Page

As you see, you can create a webpage without knowing any code. Just describe what you want to see. For example: "Create a simple page with a big title, a short paragraph, and a button centered underneath." Gemini reads this as a layout:

• Title at the top
  • Paragraph below it
  • Button centered
  • Clean spacing and alignment
Then it generates HTML/CSS that builds the page exactly as described.
What You Can Do With the Code
Once Gemini generates the code, you can immediately create something real:

• Preview it online by pasting it into any HTML/CSS editor
  • Save it as an .html file and open it in your browser
  • Use it as a prototype for a landing page or concept
  • Share it with teammates or friends to gather feedback
  • Add more elements by asking Gemini to update the snippet
This way, you're learning to build things with code, using Gemini as your builder!
Example: Making a Simple Web Card

If you say: "Make a web card with a photo on top, a title, and a short line of text." Gemini gives you: a small box, a top image, text underneath, and balanced spacing. You can update it easily by saying: "Make the corners rounder." or "Add a shadow." or "Use softer colors." Gemini updates the code automatically.

Welcome back! Today, you'll explore yet another one of Gemini's talents. We'll see how Gemini generates and transforms images using NanoBanana — the engine that powers the system's imagination.

NanoBanana helps Gemini understand your descriptions, apply style cues, and edit visuals with precision, even if you're not a designer. 

Let's get started!
Getting Started with NanoBanana

NanoBanana is the visual engine inside Gemini — the part responsible for turning ideas into images. When you ask Gemini to create or edit a picture, it's NanoBanana that handles the imagination, composition, lighting, and style work.

With NanoBanana, you can describe a scene, upload an image, or request edits, and the AI will generate the final artwork from your instructions. You can guide it entirely with prompts, or take a simpler route: explain what's in the image and choose a visual style from a built-in style library.
What NanoBanana Brings to Your Creativity
NanoBanana gives Gemini a fast, imaginative visual layer. It can:

• Understand detailed descriptions
  • Translate ideas into images
  • Apply lighting, style, and composition cues
  • Make consistent image sets
  • Adjust or rewrite visuals based on feedback
You focus on the idea — NanoBanana handles the imagery.
You don't need artistic terms. You can say things like:

• "A calm workspace with soft lighting."
  • "A simple icon shaped like a star."
  • "A clean banner for a presentation."
NanoBanana builds the visual interpretation from your words.

blocks.text: Building a Strong Image Prompt
As you see, Gemini responds best to prompts that include:

• The main subject
  • Mood or style
  • The setting
  • Colors or lighting
  • Level of detail
You don't need all of them, but a clear purpose helps NanoBanana shape the output for any goal.
Creating a Clean Presentation Banner
Let's look at an example. If you ask to create "a clean blue banner with simple shapes and a friendly headline area," NanoBanana interprets:

• A horizontal layout
  • Soft colors
  • Minimalist design
  • Open space for text
You get a polished banner ready to use.
Editing by Commands

It's not necessarily about creating new visuals all the way. With NanoBanana, you can also edit an existing image by simply requesting the changes.

For this, upload any picture and ask Gemini to:

• Replace objects
  • Adjust colors
  • Expand the background
  • Clean up elements
  • Change lighting
  • Remove distractions
Let's practice with this image of kids playing in the snow.

blocks.text: Images for Work, Presentations, and Marketing

NanoBanana's output can be used directly in slides, social posts, product ideas, reports, landing pages, or internal documentation. You can generate icons, banners, hero sections, diagrams, or concept art quickly!
Designing a Simple Icon Set

For example, you say, "Give me three simple icons with the same style: a laptop, a cloud, and a spark." NanoBanana creates a consistent set with matching shapes, colors, outlines, and proportions. Ideal for presentations or small UI elements.

blocks.text: Why Style Consistency Matters
When creating multiple images, consistency builds trust. NanoBanana can follow a visual guideline across outputs by:

• Copying color palettes
  • Matching shapes
  • Keeping textures similar
  • Aligning lighting
  • Reusing composition patterns
This helps you build cohesive sets.
Reusing a Style Prompt

Give Gemini a style once, then reuse it: "Use the same soft, rounded illustration style as the last image." NanoBanana continues in the same artistic direction automatically. You don't need to repeat every detail.

Create Music and Soundscapes with AI

You've seen Gemini handle text, data, and images. But there's one thing that still catches people off guard — it can create original music too.

Meet Lyria

Behind Gemini's music creation is Lyria — the engine that turns your words into sound. You won't see it as a separate tool. • "A calm morning song with acoustic guitar"

  • "A peaceful background score for a travel video"
Lyria will build the musical interpretation from your words alone.

How to Access the Music Tool
In the Gemini app, open the "Tools" menu and click the "Create Music" button — the one with the music note icon. That opens the music creation interface.
Understanding the Interface

When you open Create Music, you'll see a set of ready-made styles like 90's rap, Folk ballad, Workout, and more. Each one is a starting point you can preview and customize.

At the bottom, a prompt field lets you add your own instructions to shape the result.
Remix tracks are the fastest way to get started. Instead of building from zero, you:

1. Choose a style.
  2. Add your own description (topic, vibe, or even some lyrics).
  3. Generate a new version inspired by that base.
The selected track sets the overall vibe and instrumentation. Your prompt then refines the mood, tempo, lyrics, or atmosphere.

• Genre or era: 90s hip-hop, modern pop

Creating Music from Images

So far, you've described music in words. But words aren't the only way in. You can also hand Gemini an image and let it do the listening — this is called Image-to-Audio. Gemini analyzes the colors, mood, and composition of a photo, then composes music that matches what it sees. This is especially useful at work. Upload a slide deck, a product photo, or any visual, and Gemini composes a matching soundtrack for it.

  • Presentation themes (upload slides → create audio atmosphere)
  • Digital vision boards (upload inspiration → get motivational music)
Remember the image of kids playing in the snow from the last lesson? Let's turn that into a track.

Editing Lyrics

What do you do if the music is perfect, but the lyrics don't quite fit? You don't have to start over. Just ask Gemini to rewrite them while keeping everything else the same. Try: "Change the lyrics, but keep the rhythm, tone, and genre the same."
This is where the conversational advantage shines. Once you have a track, you can keep shaping it through chat:

• "Add a saxophone solo at the end"
  • "Make the drums louder"
  • "Speed it up and add more energy"
Gemini will adjust each time without losing what's already working. This is like collaborating with a producer who instantly understands your vision.

Want to take it even further? You can change the entire song's language with a single request. For example, if you prompt something like "Change this song to French, while keeping the rhythm, tone, and genre the same", you can get this as a result!

Keep these in mind, and you're good to go!

Best, [Your Name]" Not wrong — but it's bland, vague, and sounds like it was written by a generic assistant, not a strategic consultant.

blocks.question: What do you think is missing from this response?

Think about tasks you do repeatedly — weekly reports, content creation pipelines, analysis routines. Doesn't doing them one by one every time waste your expertise?

Well, in this lesson, you will learn to optimize these manual processes!
The Repetitive Task Problem

Imagine you're a content manager creating weekly social media posts for your company. Every Monday, you follow the same process:

Research trending topics → Draft 3 post ideas → Write captions → Generate image concepts → Review and finalize.
You might do this with five separate Gemini conversations:

• First prompt: "What are trending topics in [industry] this week?"
  • Second prompt: "Turn these into 3 post ideas"
  • Third prompt: "Write captions for each idea"
  • Fourth prompt: "Suggest images for these posts"
  • Fifth prompt: "Review these for brand consistency"
Five conversations. Constant copy-pasting between them. Seems like not the most convenient way.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Each step is fine individually, but you're the glue connecting them. That manual work repeats every time.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Context loss matters, but the real problem is that you are doing repetitive work. The process is the same weekly — it should be automated.

Research trending topics → Draft 3 post ideas → Write captions → Generate image concepts → Review and finalize.
You might do this with five separate Gemini conversations:

• First prompt: "What are trending topics in [industry] this week?"
  • Second prompt: "Turn these into 3 post ideas"
  • Third prompt: "Write captions for each idea"
  • Fourth prompt: "Suggest images for these posts"
  • Fifth prompt: "Review these for brand consistency"
Five conversations. Constant copy-pasting between them. Seems like not the most convenient way.

Solve Creative Challenges

Coming up with creative ideas that actually work is hard. Staring at a blank page, waiting for inspiration, wastes time.

So, here you'll learn to generate, refine, and polish creative concepts systematically with Gemini!
The Creative Block Problem

Let's say you're launching a new product — an eco-friendly water bottle for outdoor enthusiasts. 

Your boss asks: "What's our campaign concept?"
After 30 minutes, these are your ideas:

• "Stay hydrated, save the planet"
  • "The bottle that cares about Earth"
  • "Eco-friendly hydration for active lifestyles"
They're not wrong — but they're forgettable.

feedbackCorrect.text: That's right! These ideas are generic because they could describe any eco-friendly bottle. You need a specific creative angle.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Polish and features come later. The problem is a lack of distinctiveness — nothing makes this campaign stand out from competitors saying the same things.

options.label: Detailed information about product features and benefits
More professional marketing language and polish

blocks.question: What's missing from these campaign ideas?

blocks.text: The insight is: creative work isn't about waiting for inspiration to strike randomly. It's about structured exploration — systematically generating options, then refining the strongest ones. Two techniques unlock this: constrained brainstorming and iterative refinement.

feedbackCorrect.text: Constraints focus creativity productively; iteration evolves ideas through refinement. Together, they turn blank-page paralysis into systematic creative development.

feedbackIncorrect.text: It's not about quantity or guaranteed success — it's about process. Structure helps you generate focused options and evolve them into polished concepts.

  3. "Join the Green Movement" — Community-focused environmental messaging

blocks.text:
Effective creative constraints include:
  • Angle focus: "Emphasize [emotion/benefit/perspective]"
  • Format limitation: "Must work as 6-word tagline"
  • Audience specificity: "Appeal to [specific segment] who value [specific thing]"
  • Creative restriction: "Use a metaphor from [domain]" or "Avoid mentioning [overused concept]"
Constraints don't limit creativity — they focus it toward distinctive ideas.

Gemini can connect with your Google Workspace tools — Docs, Sheets, Gmail, and Drive — letting you create, analyze, and organize information directly inside your files instead of working in a separate chat.

To access this feature, you'll need a paid Gemini subscription.

This becomes possible thanks to two key capabilities: Workspace integration, which lets Gemini connect to your Google tools, and document automation, which helps it create, edit, and organize content for you automatically.
Connecting Gemini to Google Workspace

Before Gemini can work with your Workspace tools, you need to enable the integration.

This gives Gemini permission to access your Docs, Sheets, Drive, and Gmail when you request it.
Enabling Workspace Integration:

1. Open Gemini settings (gear icon in top right).
  2. Navigate to "Connected Apps" and then to "Google Workspace."
  3. Toggle on the tools you want Gemini to access (Docs, Sheets, Drive, Gmail).
  4. Grant permissions when prompted.
Once enabled, Gemini can reference and work with your Workspace files directly.
With integration enabled, you can open any Google Workspace tool and ask Gemini to:

• Create new Docs with specific content and formatting
  • Analyze data from Sheets and generate insights
  • Search Drive for relevant files and summarize them
  • Draft emails based on context from documents
Let's start with document creation — the most immediately useful capability.
